concepts.learning_objective: Explain how human resources are turned into human capital through investment.
Identify the economic and non-economic benefits that make people seek education.
Explain why spending on education and health is a source of human capital formation.
Explain why firms invest in on-the-job training and expect workers to stay afterwards.
Explain how expenditure on migration and on market information forms human capital.
Distinguish physical and human capital in terms of tangibility, separability and mobility.
Compare the depreciation and the private and social benefits of the two forms of capital.
Explain how human capital raises labour productivity and the ability to absorb new technology.
Evaluate the evidence on the link between human capital and economic growth, including two-way causality.
Interpret the indicators of education, health and income in Table 4.1.
Distinguish human capital (people as a means) from human development (people as ends in themselves).
Discuss whether IT-based services can make India a knowledge economy and lead to human development.
Explain why government must intervene in the education and health service markets.
Identify the organisations that facilitate institutions in the education and health sectors.
Interpret education expenditure as a share of total government expenditure and of GDP.
Recall the recommendations, acts and cess aimed at expanding education in India.
Assess why education for all remains a distant goal in India.
Explain the need to promote women's education in India using literacy data.
Analyse the steep education pyramid and unemployment among educated youth.
